question.problem:
Which of the following vector-valued functions are differentiable with respect to $t$ on $t\in (0,1)?$

$$
\begin{aligned}p(t) & =⟨2t-1,\,{t}^{2}+4,\,-{e}^{t}⟩ \\ q(t) & =⟨(t+1)^{4},\,\sqrt[3]{t},\,\operatorname{ln}⁡t⟩ \\ r(t) & =⟨3t+2,\,\operatorname{arctan}⁡t,\,{t}^{2}-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
All of these vector-valued functions are defined on $t\in (0,1).$ 

A function is differentiable on the interval $t\in (0,1)$ if and only if each component is differentiable on that interval.

Let's now consider the functions one-by-one.

- We differentiate $p(t)$ to find ${p}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{p}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t-1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+4),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{t})⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,2t,\,-{e}^{t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Since each component of ${p}^{′}(t)$ is defined on $t\in (0,1)$, we conclude that $p(t)$ is differentiable on this interval.

- Next, we differentiate $q(t)$ to find ${q}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((t+1)^{4}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt[3]{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨4(t+1)^{3},\,\frac{1}{3\sqrt[3]{{t}^{2}}},\,\frac{1}{t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Since each component of ${q}^{′}(t)$ is defined on $t\in (0,1)$, we have that $q(t)$ is differentiable on this interval.

- Finally, we differentiate $r(t)$ to find ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t+2),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-2)⟩ \\  & =⟨3,\,\frac{1}{1+{t}^{2}},\,2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Since each component of ${r}^{′}(t)$ is defined on $t\in (0,1)$, we conclude that $r(t)$ is differentiable on this interval.

Therefore, the answer is:

$\,$ All the functions are differentiable on $(0,1).$
